survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This OECD country note does not analyze student microdata from an ILSA (e.g., PISA/TIMSS/PIRLS) and therefore does not implement a sampling/replicate-weighting scheme for student achievement outcomes. The document synthesizes governance structures, responsibilities, and expenditure shares across levels of government (federal, provincial/territorial, local) using descriptive policy information and OECD compilation sources. As a result, there are no plausible values (PV) or survey-weight variables (e.g., W_FSTUWT, TOTWGT) to apply, and no complex survey design adjustments are described. For this type of policy framework note, the relevant “data preparation” is the compilation and categorisation of governance responsibilities rather than statistical weighting of respondents.

This is therefore a non-empirical policy framework/country profile rather than a statistical modeling study.

data.outcome_summary: This OECD Canada country note provides an overview of how the adult skills system is governed, focusing on the allocation of responsibilities and funding/expenditure structure across federal, provincial/territorial, and local levels. It characterises Canada as having a decentralised governance model for education, with constitutional authority over education held by provinces and territories, resulting in 13 distinct education systems. The note explains how Active Labour Market Policies (ALMPs), Continuing Education and Training (CET), and a portion of Adult Education (AE) are managed and funded primarily through bilateral Labour Market Development Agreements (LMDAs) and Workforce Development Agreements (WDAs) between the federal government and provinces/territories, while design and delivery are carried out at subnational levels. It also describes how Vocational Education and Training (VET) and Higher VET (HVET) are delivered by public and private post-secondary institutions overseen by provinces/territories, with variation across jurisdictions. No student assessment instruments, sampling, scaling, or PV-based benchmarks are used because the note is not an empirical ILSA analysis.
data.null_fields_interpretation: This extraction is sparse by design because the document is a policy country note rather than an empirical large-scale assessment study. There is no student-level dataset, no statistical model, and no ML pipeline to extract; consequently, fields such as total_students, PV handling details, missing-data procedures, and main predictive findings are not applicable. The note’s “results” are descriptive governance mappings (tables/infographics) rather than quantitative model outputs.
